newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CEOE praises companies' drive towards EMU.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CEOE praises companies' drive towards EMU.

text.p: The chairman of Spain's employers' union the CEOE said on Wednesday the economy had made great strides in becoming more competitive in the last 12 months, as European monetary and economic union (EMU) approaches.
CEOE chairman Jose Maria Cuevas said in a review this improvement was reflected in the fact exports now represent 50 percent of gross national product, compared to 37 percent five years ago.
However, he said to encourage companies to continue along this path, the government would have to focus on a number of key issues in the economy.
Unemployment, wage rises, research and development, professional training and rationalisation of the tax system are issues the government must address in particular.
Furthermore monetary policy, and the margin for interest rate cuts still available, must be used to contribute to reduction in financial costs, he said.
Cuevas said companies had so far made great efforts to clean up their balance sheets and streamline their operations, reflected in an average growth in capital goods of 6.4 percent in recent years.
Companies have benefitted from a more stable economy, lower interest rates, a stable peseta and rises on the financial markets, he said.

"All of this has allowed the continuation of our convergence process with other European member states and poses a challenge: to maintain this path of growing competitiveness with the objective of full integration of Spain in EMU," he said.
